text: You walk into a supermarket, focused on your list, just wanting to grab a few things and leave.
But then you hit the wide, open aisles. They feel spacious, almost empty, making your quick trip surprisingly longer.
You might think it's for comfort, or to accommodate more carts. But is it really just about giving you space, or is something else at play?
The truth is, these wide aisles are a carefully designed system. They slow your pace, forcing your eyes to wander, increasing exposure to everything.
This deliberate pacing makes you browse more, pick up items you didn't plan for, and ultimately spend more than you intended.
The next time you're in a store, you'll still feel the calm of wide aisles, but now you'll see the invisible hand guiding your cart.
